title: Short Stuff: China's Corpse Walkers
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the Chinese tradition of corpse walking (corpse walkers) and corpse herding, in which Taoist priests led dead bodies home for burial, mostly in Hunan Province and the Xiangxi region. Topics include the belief that dying away from home produces a restless spirit, the reanimation claim involving a black cat's static electricity, the bamboo-pole setups used in each method, and an account by Louise Hung about her grandfather's childhood sighting posted on the Order of the Good Death website. They note the tradition's roots in the Qing dynasty (dating to 1616 per Chuck) and reports that Mao suppressed it in the 1960s as superstitious. The episode also includes off-topic banter about Chuck's new kitten Olivia and his Halloween costume idea.

segments.title: Opening and setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the Spooky Month episode on a Halloween-adjacent Chinese custom and set up the Hunan/Xiangxi context and the belief that people dying away from home must be returned for burial.

segments.name: x
segments.title: Origins of the custom and its suppression
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh explain the remedy of walking the corpse home and note the tradition's roots in the Qing dynasty and its suppression under Mao as superstitious.

segments.title: Taoist priests and corpse walking
segments.summary: Taoist priests walked corpses home; in corpse walking a single priest reanimated a corpse to walk behind him, guided by lantern light and calls of directions.

segments.title: Runners, gongs, and the black cat
segments.summary: Runners warned villages with a gong; the priest was accompanied by a black cat that rubbed on the corpse, with the claim that its static electricity reanimated the body.

segments.title: Chuck's kitten Olivia
segments.summary: Chuck shares a personal update about rescuing and adopting kitten Olivia, which is off-topic from the custom.

segments.title: Corpse herding overview
segments.summary: Corpse herding moved multiple corpses at once, with several priests and runners, likened by Chuck to a halftime dancer with rods.

segments.title: Louise Hung's grandfather's account
segments.summary: Josh recounts Louise Hung's account, posted on the Order of the Good Death website, of her grandfather and brother seeing a line of corpses lurching through town to a gong.

segments.title: Bamboo pole mechanics of corpse walking
segments.summary: The hosts describe that the solo corpse walker carried a corpse on their back, tied to a bamboo pole with a black robe draped over both, so the corpse appeared to walk.

segments.title: Corpse herding bamboo poles and closing jokes
segments.summary: Corpses were tied by the arms to horizontal poles carried by front and back priests, making them bounce and appear to walk in line; the hosts joke about Halloween costumes.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh closes the short stuff episode and the show's production credit is read.
